claims.subject: olog

claims.quote: The term is due to Spivak & Kent's "Ologs: A Categorical Framework for Knowledge Representation"

claims.subject: olog
claims.value: asserted, not assumed
claims.quote: **Commutativity is asserted, not assumed.**

claims.subject: trace-difference
claims.quote: sit at least three independent sources of difference

claims.subject: sameness-hierarchy
claims.value: a witness of a stronger relation is a witness of every weaker one; the converse is false
claims.quote: A witness of a stronger relation is automatically a witness of every weaker one (a literal identification trivially gives the invertible map, the deformation, the bound, …); the converse is false

claims.subject: univalence-axiom
claims.quote: Under the **univalence axiom** this becomes literal: for types in a universe $\mathcal{U}$, an equality in $\mathcal{U}$ *is* an equivalence, so $(x =_{\mathcal{U}} y) \simeq (x \simeq y)$.

claims.subject: sheaf-condition
claims.value: for every admissible cover, compatible local sections have one unique global section
claims.quote: **for every admissible cover and every family of local sections on it that agree on every overlap, there is one and only one global section restricting to them.**

claims.subject: sheaf-condition
claims.quote: $$F(c) \;\simeq\; F(c_1) \times_{F(c_1 \times_c c_2)} F(c_2).$$

claims.subject: pullback
claims.value: object of agreements X ×_Z Y
claims.quote: The pullback *is* the object of agreements.

claims.subject: grothendieck-topology
claims.value: rule for which families count as covers, stable under pullback, closed under refinement and composition
claims.quote: Equipping $\mathcal{C}$ with a rule for which families count as covers (one that is stable under pullback, closed under refinement, and closed under composition) is a **Grothendieck topology** $J$; the pair $(\mathcal{C}, J)$ is a **site**

claims.subject: cech-nerve
claims.value: degree 0 patches; degree 1 pairwise overlaps; degree 2 triple overlaps
claims.quote: a simplicial object that in degree $0$ lists the patches, in degree $1$ lists pairwise overlaps, in degree $2$ lists triple overlaps, and so on

claims.subject: infinity-sheaf
claims.value: sheaf-like object valued in infinity-groupoids with coherent equivalence on overlaps
claims.quote: An **$\infty$-sheaf** is a sheaf-like object valued in $\infty$-groupoids instead of sets: instead of *equality* on overlaps one requires *coherent equivalence*, with the coherence tracked at every level.

claims.subject: admissible-cover
claims.value: G is a model of c_acc, not of c
claims.quote: The limit $G = \lim F$ over such a cover reconstructs a model of that interface, *not* of $c$

claims.subject: sellars1956empiricism
claims.value: empirical knowledge is rational because self-correcting, not because it has a foundation
claims.quote: For empirical knowledge, like its sophisticated extension, science, is rational, not because it has a foundation but because it is a self-correcting enterprise which can put any claim in jeopardy, though not all at once.

claims.subject: foundationalism
claims.value: a privileged class of transitions that need no prior justification
claims.quote: there *must* be a privileged class of transitions that need no prior justification

claims.subject: coherence-theory-of-truth
claims.value: Bradley, Blanshard, BonJour
claims.quote: It is the central claim of the coherence theory of truth (Bradley, Blanshard, BonJour)

claims.subject: bonjour-structure-empirical-knowledge
claims.value: The Structure of Empirical Knowledge
claims.quote: BonJour's *Structure of Empirical Knowledge*

claims.subject: wordless-introspection
claims.value: immediate pre-conceptual awareness in which trace and topic coincide
claims.quote: In the immediate, pre-conceptual awareness of one's own experience, before it is named, categorised, or compared, the trace and the topic coincide.

claims.subject: hacking1983representing
claims.value: representing and intervening are the two epistemic relations to the world
claims.quote: representing is not the only epistemic relation we have to the world; *intervening* — doing something to the world, observing the difference, and so getting evidence about what is really there — is the other half

claims.subject: transformer-residual
claims.value: H_{l+1} = H_l + F_theta(H_l)
claims.quote: H_{\ell+1} = H_\ell + F_\theta(H_\ell)

claims.subject: multi-head-attention
claims.value: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V
claims.quote: \mathrm{Attn}(Q,K,V) = \mathrm{softmax}\!\Bigl(\tfrac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\Bigr)V

claims.subject: coherent-difference-procedure
claims.quote: Compressed into nine steps you can run through on any dataset, in any domain.

claims.subject: coherent-difference-analogy
claims.value: a useful analogy is not a theorem
claims.quote: A useful analogy is not a theorem.

claims.subject: toposes-as-bridges
claims.value: the same topos admits several presentations and invariant facts transfer
claims.quote: the same topos admits several presentations — as a sheaf topos over different sites, as the classifying topos of a geometric theory — and the facts invariant under that equivalence transfer between them

claims.subject: tarski-correspondence
claims.value: a coherent model is true at licensed contact points with the world
claims.quote: by joining that discipline to Tarski's correspondence, so that a coherent model is *true* (not merely internally consistent) at every licensed contact point with the world.

claims.subject: tarski-wahrheitsbegriff
claims.quote: In 1935 (the German-language paper "Der Wahrheitsbegriff in den formalisierten Sprachen", published in *Studia Philosophica*

claims.subject: tarski-wahrheitsbegriff-polish

qualifiers.title: Pojęcie prawdy w językach nauk dedukcyjnych

claims.quote: the Polish original "Pojęcie prawdy w językach nauk dedukcyjnych" had appeared in 1933

claims.subject: tarski-convention-t
claims.value: A sentence x of a language L is true in L if, and only if, p, where p is a meta-language sentence that expresses the same meaning as x.
claims.quote: A sentence $\boldsymbol{x}$ of a language $\mathcal{L}$ is *true in $\mathcal{L}$* if, and only if, $p$, where $p$ is any sentence of the meta-language which "expresses the same meaning" as $\boldsymbol{x}$.

claims.subject: anomaly
claims.value: constraints not yet integrated, not defeats
claims.quote: \boxed{\text{Anomalies are constraints not yet integrated, not defeats.}}

claims.subject: structural-realism
claims.value: what is preserved across theory change is the structure of the equations, not the ontology of unobservables
claims.quote: proposed \emph{structural realism} as the philosophical position that takes seriously the chain's signature fact: across theory change (Fresnel → Maxwell, classical → relativistic), what is preserved is not the ontology of unobservables but the *structure* of the equations that relate them

claims.subject: ontic-structural-realism
claims.value: there is nothing but structure; the world is the chain of admissible cover systems
claims.quote: not "we only know the structure" but "there *is* nothing but the structure" — the world *is* the chain of admissible cover systems, not a thing-in-itself behind them

claims.subject: goodman-irrealism
claims.value: there are no ready-made worlds and no minds constructing them from nothing; there are many worlds made by different symbol systems
claims.quote: there are no "ready-made worlds" *and* no minds constructing them from nothing — there are *many* worlds, made by different symbol systems, each as legitimate in its own right as any other

claims.subject: bradley-appearance-and-reality
claims.quote: F. H. Bradley's *Appearance and Reality*\citeauthor{bradley1893appearance} \citeyear{bradley1893appearance}

claims.subject: bradley-coherence-theory
claims.value: Truth is the systematic coherence of ideas, determined ultimately by the nature of the idea or the reality it represents.
claims.quote: Truth, we may say, is the systematic coherence of ideas, such coherence being determined ultimately by the nature of the idea itself, or by the reality which the idea endeavours to represent.

claims.subject: blanshard-coherence-theory
claims.value: The truth of a proposition is its coherence with the whole of experience and ultimately with the whole of reality.
claims.quote: The truth of a proposition is nothing but its coherence with the whole of experience, and ultimately with the whole of reality.

claims.subject: coherence
claims.value: descent on admissible covers
claims.quote: \boxed{\;\text{coherence} \;\stackrel{\text{def.}}{=}\; \text{descent on admissible covers}.\;}

claims.subject: rosetta-stone
claims.quote: The Rosetta Stone (Decree of Memphis, 196 B.C.)

claims.subject: mercury-perihelion-precession
claims.quote: the anomalous precession of Mercury's perihelion, about $43$ arcseconds per century

claims.subject: general-relativity
claims.quote: General relativity — \citeauthor{einstein1916foundation}'s (\citeyear{einstein1916foundation}) \citetitle{einstein1916foundation}

claims.subject: first-order-model-theory
claims.value: a consistent first-order theory admits a model
claims.quote: by completeness and compactness, a consistent first-order theory admits a model, so "no contradiction is derivable" literally guarantees "there exists a structure in which every theorem holds"

claims.subject: popper-falsificationism
claims.value: a scientific theory earns its status from risky predictions that would refute it if they failed
claims.quote: insisted that a scientific theory earns its status not from the accumulation of confirmations but from *risky* predictions — claims that, if they failed at a contact point, would refute it

claims.subject: dappled-world
claims.value: the clean laws of idealised model setups are only approximately true of the messy, multifactorial world
claims.quote: the clean laws of the idealised model setups are true of the clean setups and only approximately true of the messy, multifactorial world we actually want to know about

claims.subject: self-consistent-fantasy
claims.value: coherent model whose Tarski if-and-only-if fails at contact points although every arrow is licensed
claims.quote: Tarski's if-and-only-if fails at the contact points even though every arrow in the diagram is licensed. Result: a perfectly coherent fiction.

claims.subject: factbook
claims.value: individually true claims with no internal structure; descent fails and there is no global model
claims.quote: the model has no internal structure: its claims do not fit together, descent fails, the "global model" is a heap of disconnected facts. Result: a factbook.

claims.subject: calibrated-error
claims.value: coherent and licensed model with a small, consistent systematic bias in its calibration
claims.quote: the calibration is systematically, slightly off. The model's outputs track the world closely enough to be useful, but with a small, consistent bias that no single contact point reveals.

claims.subject: out-of-cover-query
claims.value: query lies outside the accessible region c_acc, so no licensed contact point exists
claims.quote: the *query* lies outside $c_{\mathrm{acc}}$, in a region the cover never reached. There is then *no* licensed bridge to check

claims.subject: llm-inference
claims.value: no live world-to-representation observation arrow at inference; only internal transitions
claims.quote: The LLM, *at inference and by default*, has no live $W\to R_i$ arrow of its own

claims.subject: emergent-capabilities
claims.value: few-shot in-context learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, code generation, and instruction following appear discontinuously at scale
claims.quote: Some LLM behaviours appear discontinuously at scale: few-shot in-context learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, code generation, instruction following

claims.subject: formal-verification
claims.value: type-checking a proof in Coq or Lean is the strongest currently available Tarski check
claims.quote: the strongest Tarski check currently available is type-checking a proof in an interactive theorem prover: **Coq** \cite{bertot2013coq} or **Lean** \cite{moura2015lean}

claims.subject: rlhf
claims.value: tunes a policy to maximise a reward model that encodes human preference; the rater's preference is a fact in W
claims.quote: RLHF adds admissible transitions to *human preferences*. The reward model encodes what humans find helpful and harmless; the policy is tuned to maximise that reward.
